title: Zuno Experience Client Declaration (OKF v0.3 frontmatter + Zuno extension)
description: Schema for the YAML frontmatter of experience-clients/<name>/client.okf.md (zuno-demo ADR-0592). An experience client is a user interface over the governed chain (zuno-demo ADR-0587: Open WebUI, OpenClaw) that calls the mcp-gateway on behalf of a signed-in user under a logical agent name (X-Zuno-Agent). It is NOT an agent: it has no graph, prompt, RAG, UI tile or model preference, and it never becomes a UnifAI bundle, a Keycloak agent_* group, a MaaS subscription, an A2A endpoint or a delegation target. This declaration only says which callers may use the logical name (access.groups, business groups) and which tools each of its tasks allows (tasks/<task>.md, the ordinary task schema). The five-factor decision of the mcp-gateway still applies to every tool: the caller's groups and the request classification are checked against policies/tools/tool-policy.yaml.

okf_version.description: [OKF CORE] OKF envelope version this document conforms to.

type.description: [OKF CORE] Document kind. Always "experience-client" for client.okf.md files.

description.description: [OKF CORE] One or two sentence summary of the client and what its tools are for.

zuno.description: [ZUNO EXT] What the mcp-gateway needs to entitle the logical agent name.

name.description: The logical agent name the client sends as X-Zuno-Agent. Matches the experience-clients/<name> directory and must not be the name of an agent.

tasks.description: Task names the client sends as X-Zuno-Task; each is experience-clients/<name>/tasks/<task>.md (zuno-okf-task-v0.3.schema.json). Only allowed_tools is read.

classification.description: The data classification the client declares on its requests (descriptive; the client's deployment sets the X-Zuno-Data-Classification header). Its tasks should only allow tools whose min_classification it reaches.

access.description: Who may use the logical agent name.

groups.description: Keycloak `zuno` realm groups (JWT `groups` claim, without the leading slash) whose members may call the mcp-gateway under this name. Unlike an agent, an experience client serves every employee, so these are business groups (sales, consultant, ...), not an agent_* entitlement group; the tool policy still narrows each tool to its own allowed_groups.
